title: I Was Separated From My Position at Webflow
content:
The morning I got let go, I saw a new post on the Webflow blog while taking my coffee doing my routine readings. The headline read, "A Message to the Webflow Team," and it announced that the company was making cuts. "Weird," I thought. Just thirty minutes later, a separation meeting appeared on my calendar. That morning felt surreal. Everything happened so fast. It's taken days to process the whirlwind of emotions. On one hand, there’s a deep sense of loss as I part ways with one of the most empathetic and passionate teams I've ever been part of. On the other, there’s immense pride and satisfaction. I had the freedom to innovate, experiment, and grow as a professional designer during my time there. The past few days have felt like navigating through fog in a high-stakes environment because now I'm facing the unknown. As I begin to look forward, I pausing to reflect.

Looking back over the past three years, I’m filled with pride and satisfaction. The design files and team sessions where I invested my highest care and focus—whether it was dramatic video productions that pushed the brand's boundaries or the pixel-perfect details of webinar asset kits—show how far-reaching my influence was within the marketing organization. I'm grateful to the leaders and coaches who supported me throughout this journey and advocated for us to try new things. Reflecting on moments of collaboration, where abstract ideas turned into beautiful executions, brings me a smile and happiness. The accolades and positive feedback from stakeholders and the Webflow community were affirmations of our collective effort. Though this chapter ends on a bittersweet note, the confidence and joy from our achievements provide a solid foundation as I look forward to new opportunities. I’m optimistic and eager to apply the lessons and skills I've developed, knowing that this chapter has seen me change in entirely new ways.
